A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HALO, with matching core methods and experiments. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning accuracies, gradient-sensitivity analyses, HALO-level ablations, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds placement ablations, Qwen evaluations, C4 pretraining, MXFP6 experiments, and inference timings.

M1.justification: The FFT, PEFT, and HQ-FSDP procedures remain unchanged; HALO-0 is mainly renamed No-HALO. Appendix A.9 adds an inference adaptation that fuses Hadamard transformations into preceding linear modules, retaining explicit transforms before attention output and MLP down projections.

E1.justification: The ViGGO, GSM8K, and SQL fine-tuning tasks are retained. v3 Appendix A.14 adds language-model pretraining on C4, substantially extending the evaluated task coverage beyond downstream fine-tuning. The Qwen and MXFP6 experiments otherwise reuse existing tasks.

E2.justification: v3 Table 1 adds SwitchBack and Jetfire to the FP8 accuracy comparison, where v1 Table 3 reported only HALO-0 alongside BF16. Conversely, SwitchBack is omitted from the single-GPU transformer-block runtime comparison in v3 Table 7. DeepSeek is discussed but has no separately identified experimental result.

E3.justification: v3 adds Qwen-2.5 14B/32B configurations, TinyLlama-1.1B pretraining on 22B tokens with evaluation loss, eight-GPU end-to-end timing configurations, and an inference benchmark. It also adds FP8 PEFT, MXFP6 fine-tuning, and FP4 pretraining settings. The original three-task fine-tuning hyperparameters and dataset splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 Figure 6 substantially expands the ablation from three selected HALO levels to combinations of forward, input-gradient, and weight-gradient transformations. Figure 5 adds distribution diagnostics for activations, errors, and weights. The original gradient-cosine analysis and three-level accuracy ablation are retained, with the latter moved to Appendix A.8.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five seeds and report accuracy means with standard errors. Timing averages retain 100 measurements plus 20 warm-ups for linear layers and 30 plus 10 for blocks. No changed repetition policy, confidence-interval procedure, or significance testing is reported.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial accuracy, inference, and pretraining results, including INT8/FP4 pretraining divergence. Under the retained four-GPU, batch-size-four setup, reported INT8 end-to-end speedup changes from 1.29x to 1.35x; the new eight-GPU setting reaches 1.41x. Some accuracy entries change beyond rounding: HALO-2 GSM8K becomes 68.3 in v3 Table 1 versus 68.15 in v1 Table 2, although v3 Table 5 retains 68.15.

T1.justification: v3 Appendix A.1 adds a normalization-Jacobian derivation and an argument that forward-pass transformation absorption does not extend to the backward pass. The stated Hadamard design-space count also changes from 24 modes to 512. Existing HALO and PEFT computation equations are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The central claim of accurate, accelerated low-precision FFT and PEFT remains. The abstract shifts its headline novelty claim from maintaining FP8 accuracy to INT8/FP6 accuracy and raises the advertised maximum end-to-end speedup from 1.31x to 1.41x. The introduction also extends its stated validation to Qwen models.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations for prioritizing input-gradient protection over weight-gradient protection, citing error propagation and transpose overhead. It also introduces the claimed RMSNorm obstacle to transformation absorption and attributes declining inference speedup at batch size 16 to attention becoming a bottleneck. Existing outlier and communication interpretations largely persist.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit HALO code-repository link and configuration information for its new experiments. Existing hyperparameters and HQ-FSDP implementation details are mostly relocated unchanged. However, v1's disclosure of 64 NCCL threads and enabled forward/backward prefetching is absent from v3.

R1.justification: v3 adds DeepSeek-V3 to contextualize established FP8 pretraining and sharpen the INT8/FP6 motivation. It expands discussion of computational invariance with SliceGPT and adds references supporting Qwen, TinyLlama, and compute-optimal pretraining. The broad positioning against inference quantization, SwitchBack, and Jetfire remains.

P1.justification: The title and introduction are rewritten, related work is integrated into Background, and the method narrative is reorganized into challenges and solution steps. PEFT equations/results, hyperparameters, and existing ablations move into a substantially reorganized appendix. These are extensive structural and explanatory changes beyond the newly added experiments.

P2.justification: The document changes from a predominantly two-column layout to a single-column layout. Outlier visualizations are replaced and expanded, the method/FSDP schematic is redesigned, accuracy tables are consolidated, and several runtime bar charts become appendix tables. New heatmaps, distribution plots, and experimental tables substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's selected-level ablation and Llama-focused evaluations, v3 provides useful additional support through broader placement testing, larger-model comparisons, MXFP6 results, and explicit pretraining failures. The code link also improves reproducibility information. These gains are partly offset by unreconciled results: Figure 6 reports GSM8K HALO-1 accuracy of 67.05 while retained Table 5 gives 62.27, and end-to-end speedup summaries disagree with Table 2. The net improvement is therefore limited.
